en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Seventh Chapter
The Discussion on Resultant and that Which is Subject to Ripening:
Is it the case that what is resultant is also subject to ripening?
Yes, it is.
Is its result a phenomenon subject to ripening?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is its result a phenomenon subject to ripening?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then for each and every one of them, there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the round, and no parinibbāna through non-clinging?
You should not speak thus… [and so on].
Is that which is a result also a phenomenon subject to ripening? Yes.
Are "result" and "phenomenon subject to ripening" identical, one in meaning, the same, of equal status, and of the same nature? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the result a phenomenon that has the nature of ripening? Yes.

Is it the case that the resultant (vipāka), the state subject to result (vipākadhammadhamma), and the resultant itself— being conascent, co-nascent, conjoined, associated, arising together, ceasing together, having the same basis,
and having the same object— are all such? One should not say so… [and so on]… Is the resultant the state subject to result?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that very unwholesome state itself the result of the unwholesome, and that very wholesome state itself the result of the wholesome?
You should not speak thus … [as before] … .
Is it the case that what is a result is also a phenomenon subject to ripening? Yes.

Is it then the case that by the very same consciousness with which one kills a living being, one is cooked in hell; and by the very same consciousness with which one gives a gift, one rejoices in heaven?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Should it not be said that "resultant is a state subject to result"?
“Yes.
“But are not the four resultant immaterial aggregates mutual conditions for one another?
“Yes.”
If the four formless aggregates that are results are related to one another by way of mutuality condition, then indeed, sir, you must say:
"A result is a phenomenon subject to result.
The discussion on whether a result is a phenomenon subject to result is concluded.
The Seventh Chapter.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
Compendium, association, mental state, mental generosity, and merit consisting in enjoyment increases.
"By what is given here, they subsist there; the earth is the result of kamma, aging and death are the result; there is no result of the noble Dhamma;
the result is a phenomenon subject to the nature of being a result."
